facts.text: Anderson earned the nicknames "Electric City" and "Friendliest City in South Carolina," a testament to its early power plant and welcoming spirit.
In 1851 the Johnson Female Seminary opened in Anderson, becoming Johnson University a year later and marking the town’s first higher‑education institution.
Growth accelerated in 1856 when the Greenville and Columbia Railroad reached Anderson, linking the town to regional commerce.
Whitner’s 1895 hydroelectric plant on the Rocky River generated high‑voltage power, earning Anderson the title Electric City and pioneering U.S. high‑voltage generation.
In 1908 a new library and hospital opened, expanding Anderson’s public services during the early twentieth century.
Anderson became the first city worldwide to supply a cotton gin with electricity, showcasing its industrial innovation in the late nineteenth century.
